lesson.subtitle: Lesson 1 -- The Room Where the Song Gets Made
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Pedro Henrique Tadeu Alves da Silva | Lesson 1 -- The Room Where the Song Gets Made

listenings.text: Welcome to the course. Before the first class, here is how this one works, because it is not a lecture. Every week you bring something. It can be eight bars, it can be a single verse, it can be a rough voice memo recorded on your phone at two in the morning. You post it, and the rest of the group listens to it before we meet. Then, in the live session, we talk about it. And I mean talk. I am going to ask you what the song is trying to do, and you are going to answer in your own words, out loud, in front of eleven strangers. That part frightens people, so let me be honest about it. Nobody here is grading your accent. What we are listening for is whether you can say why you made a choice. If you can tell me why the second verse is shorter than the first, you are doing exactly what this course asks for. Every week somebody says, my English is not good enough for this. And every week that person turns out to be the one with the most interesting reason.

People ask what I do and I still do not have a clean answer, so I usually give them the long one. I sit between two departments. On one side there is the picture, the cameras, the edit, the show going out on a Sunday night. On the other side there is the music, the band, the arrangements, the backing tracks the singers perform over. My job is the place where those two things have to agree. Right now, for example, I am working on a new season, and this week that means three things at the same time. I am building the backing tracks for the live shows. I am sitting in rehearsals with a notebook, because that is where you find out that a key is wrong for somebody. And I am on the phone with the picture team about a cue that runs four seconds long. None of that appears in a job title. So when somebody at a party asks me what I do, I say I make sure the music and the pictures arrive at the same second. It is not the whole truth, but it is the part that makes sense to a stranger in ten words.

extra_audio.text: Pedro works between audiovisual production and music production. He works on music shows: The Voice, Masked Singer and X Factor. Right now he is building the backing tracks for a new season. This week he is also sitting in rehearsals with the band. On the side, he produces his own projects. Then he asks the other person what they are working on at the moment.
